staging_order.instructions: Cells are in time order, labelled with frame numbers. Expected order: {expected_order}. How far is this sequence from a clean one-at-a-time arrival order, where each element finishes arriving before the next one starts?
criteria: Every element finishes arriving before the next one starts, in the expected order
Order is correct, but one element is still settling as the next one starts
One element starts while the previous element is still visibly arriving
Two or more elements arrive at once, or an element arrives clearly out of order

dead_frame.instructions: Is this frame essentially empty: a flat background with at most one small mark and nothing a viewer can read?

pop.instructions: This is a difference image of two consecutive frames inside a transition (not a hard cut). Bright areas changed between the two frames. Does a large part of the picture change in this single step, so that it would read as a pop or glitch instead of smooth motion?

abrupt_change.instructions: This is a difference image of two frames a few milliseconds apart. Bright areas changed. Does a large part of the picture change at once (a pop or a hard fill), instead of a small object moving?

overlap.instructions: Does any text sit on top of other text or on a busy graphic so that a word is hard to read, or does a moving shape or card cross a label?

legible_feed.instructions: This frame is shown at phone-feed size. Ignore decorative text that is part of an object, texture or background. All other on-screen text counts, including small labels, tags and numbers. Is any such word blurred, merged with another line, or too small to read without zooming?

ui_occlusion.instructions: This frame has translucent red boxes shaded over the APPROXIMATE areas where the platform's interface (buttons, captions, icons) typically covers the video (community-measured zones; exact placement varies by device and app version). Is any text or key graphic inside the shaded red zones?

text_integrity.instructions: Is any on-screen word partly hidden, split into two colours, overlapped by another word, or followed by a stray fragment of text, so that a word could be misread as another word or looks broken?

hierarchy.instructions: How unclear is the reading order of this frame? Higher means worse.
criteria: One obvious read path; tiers clearly separated by size, weight and space
Clear order; tiers distinct; minor crowding
Readable order, but two tiers look nearly the same size or weight
Entry point exists but the second read is ambiguous
No clear entry point; elements compete equally
